newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin congratulates former arch-foe Rutskoi.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin congratulates former arch-foe Rutskoi.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Thursday gritted his teeth and sent a short telegram of congratulations to former arch-foe Alexander Rutskoi, the man who tried to overthrow him in October 1993.
Rutskoi bounced back from political oblivion on Monday when he was elected governor of the central Kursk region and gained a seat in the Federation Council upper chamber of parliament.
In such cases congratulations are in order and Yeltsin obliged, but in doing so he managed to take a swipe at his former deputy.

"I hope your actions in this important post will help stabilise the socio-economic situation in the region," said the telegram sent to a man who led a revolt by parliamentary deputies in which around 140 people were killed.
None of the telegrams Yeltsin sent to other victorious governors carried the same phrase.
Rutskoi struck a conciliatory note after his win by saying he did not intend to "wage war with the Kremlin".

Yeltsin chose the Afghan war hero as his running mate in 1991 to win over the votes of reformist communists and the military. But Rutskoi later took the side of the conservative parliament in a power struggle with the Russian leader.
The 1993 uprising only ended when government tanks shelled the parliament building. Rutskoi and other opponents were jailed, but the new parliament pardoned them in 1994.
